findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates every `CalendarCache` row for the credential without filtering on `expiresAt`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. Expired rows are not deleted elsewhere, so `cacheUpdatedAt` stays non-null after the cache expires. The UI then shows “Cache Status / Last updated” and “Delete cached data” for a cache that is not actually being served, giving users a misleading view of cache state. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` predicate or return expiry state explicitly.

findings.title: Migration backfills every cache row with the deployment time
findings.body: Adding `updatedAt ... DEFAULT NOW()` sets all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows to the time the migration runs. Since the new UI displays `_max(updatedAt)` as “Last updated”, every existing cached credential will appear to have been refreshed at deploy time even though the old rows have no real update timestamp. Existing caches will report a false freshness date until each row is rewritten. Consider making the column nullable for legacy rows, backfilling from a meaningful source, or suppressing the status for backfilled rows.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connected calendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and `onSuccess` is optional at this component’s API. In a caller that does not pass an invalidating `onSuccess`, the dropdown continues to render the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and a delete action for data that no longer exists until the user manually refreshes. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` after successful deletion.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US
findings.body: The component formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the active locale from `useLocale`. Users in other locales get U.S.-formatted dates in an otherwise localized UI. Use the current locale or a shared date formatting helper instead of the literal `"en-US"`.

findings.title: Webhook test script uses macOS-only sed syntax
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed on Linux interprets the empty string incorrectly and fails or behaves unpredictably, so the script cannot update `.env` on Linux. Separately, `ENV_FILE` on line 5 is relative to the caller’s current working directory, so running it from the repo root writes to the parent directory’s `.env` rather than the repo `.env`. Use a portable in-place edit and resolve paths relative to the script location.

findings.title: No tests for destructive cache deletion authorization
findings.body: This PR adds a destructive `deleteCache` mutation and an ownership check, but no tests cover the new handler, the unauthorized path (credential id belonging to another user), or the repository’s `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` behavior (empty ids, multiple cache rows, expired rows). A regression in the ownership check would let a user delete another user’s cache. Add unit/integration tests for authorized and unauthorized deletion and the cache-status query.
